children: U.S. crude oil inventories rose more than expected in a second consecutive weekly build, according to data released Wednesday by the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve were up by 3.4 million barrels, at 417.8 million barrels, in the week ended Nov. 13 and were about 3% below the five-year average for the time of year, the EIA said. Crude stocks were expected to have risen by 1 million barrels, according to a Wall Street Journal survey of analysts.
Oil stored in the SPR fell by 3.2 million barrels, to 276.4 million barrels. Oil stocks at Cushing, Okla., the Nymex delivery hub, were down by 1.2 million barrels, at 26.1 million barrels.

The EIA estimated U.S. crude oil production at 14 million barrels a day, up by 19,000 barrels a day from the previous week. Crude oil imports fell by 1.1 million barrels a day, to 5.6 million barrels a day, while exports rose by 1 million barrels a day, to 4.5 million barrels a day.

Refineries ran at 95.7% of capacity, up from 95.2% the previous week, although crude input to refineries fell by 129,000 barrels a day, to 16.9 million barrels a day. Refinery runs were forecast to have risen by one fifth of a percentage point in the Journal survey.

Gasoline inventories increased by 5.2 million barrels, to 215.9 million barrels, compared with expectations of a 1.4 million barrel build, and were 3% above the five-year average for the time of year. Gasoline demand was 8.8 million barrels a day, up by 23,000 barrels a day from the previous week.

Distillate fuel stocks were up by 1.6 million barrels, at 104.9 million barrels, or 7% below the five-year average for the time of year. Distillate inventories were forecast to have risen by 500,000 barrels.

Change in U.S. oil inventories for the week ended Nov. 13: 
 
                   Crude       Gasoline      Distillates        Refinery Use 
EIA data:           3.4           5.2            1.6                 0.5 
Forecast:           1.0           1.4            0.5                 0.2
Note: Numbers in millions of barrels, with the exception of refinery use, which is in percentage points.
